continents.name: Africa
continents.description: The cradle of humanity — home to the Sahara, the Nile, and the savanna.

continents.name: Antarctica
continents.description: The frozen southernmost continent — no countries, just research stations.

continents.name: Asia
continents.description: The largest and most populous continent — home to the world's highest peak, Mount Everest.

continents.name: Europe
continents.description: A continent of many small countries packed with old cities, castles, and rivers.

continents.name: North America
continents.description: From the Arctic to the Caribbean — home of the Grand Canyon and the Great Lakes.

continents.name: Oceania
continents.description: Australia plus thousands of Pacific islands.

continents.name: South America
continents.description: Home to the Amazon rainforest and the Andes mountains.

countries.name: United States
countries.fact_card: Spans four time zones in the mainland and includes the world's first national park, Yellowstone.

countries.name: Canada
countries.fact_card: The world's second-largest country by area, with more lakes than the rest of the world combined.

countries.name: Mexico
countries.fact_card: Home of the ancient Maya and Aztec civilizations and the birthplace of chocolate.

countries.name: Brazil
countries.fact_card: Holds most of the Amazon rainforest and is the only country in South America that speaks Portuguese.

countries.name: Argentina
countries.fact_card: Stretches from subtropical jungle in the north to the icy edge of Antarctica in the south.

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.official_name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
countries.fact_card: An island nation made of four countries: England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.

countries.name: France
countries.fact_card: The world's most-visited country, with mountains, coastlines, and overseas territories on five continents.

countries.name: Germany
countries.fact_card: Once split in two by a wall through Berlin; reunified in 1990.

countries.name: Spain
countries.fact_card: Sits on the Iberian Peninsula and once ruled an empire that spanned the Americas.

countries.name: Italy
countries.fact_card: Shaped like a boot kicking the island of Sicily; home of the Roman Empire.

countries.name: Russia
countries.fact_card: The largest country on Earth, stretching across 11 time zones.

countries.name: China
countries.fact_card: Home to the world's longest wall and, for centuries, the world's largest population.

countries.name: Japan
countries.fact_card: A chain of more than 14,000 islands; the sun on its flag represents Japan as 'land of the rising sun.'

countries.name: India
countries.fact_card: The world's most populous democracy and home to 22 official languages.

countries.name: South Korea
countries.fact_card: Famous worldwide for K-pop and K-dramas; shares a tense border with North Korea.

countries.name: Saudi Arabia
countries.fact_card: Holds Islam's two holiest cities, Mecca and Medina, and vast deserts of sand and oil.

countries.name: Egypt
countries.fact_card: Built one of the world's oldest civilizations along the Nile, the longest river on Earth.

countries.name: South Africa
countries.fact_card: Has three capital cities and is home to the world's deepest gold mines.

countries.name: Nigeria
countries.fact_card: Africa's most populous country, with over 500 languages spoken.

countries.name: Australia
countries.fact_card: Both a country and a continent — home to kangaroos, koalas, and the Great Barrier Reef.

countries.name: Netherlands
countries.fact_card: About a third of the country lies below sea level, protected by an enormous system of dikes.

countries.name: Sweden
countries.fact_card: One of the most forested countries in Europe, with a coastline scattered with 30,000 islands.

countries.name: Norway
countries.fact_card: Carved by glaciers, Norway's coast is a maze of fjords and one of the world's longest coastlines.

countries.name: Poland
countries.fact_card: Home to Europe's last primeval forest and the birthplace of scientist Marie Curie.

countries.name: Portugal
countries.fact_card: From this small country, explorers like Vasco da Gama opened up sea routes around the world.

countries.name: Greece
countries.fact_card: Birthplace of the Olympic Games and home to over 6,000 islands scattered across two seas.

countries.name: Switzerland
countries.fact_card: A landlocked alpine nation famous for neutrality, chocolate, and four official languages.

countries.name: Indonesia
countries.fact_card: An archipelago of more than 17,000 islands — the world's largest island nation.

countries.name: Thailand
countries.fact_card: Known as the 'Land of Smiles' — the only Southeast Asian country never colonized by Europeans.

countries.name: Vietnam
countries.fact_card: An S-shaped country along the South China Sea, famous for rice terraces and pho noodle soup.

countries.name: Turkey
countries.fact_card: Bridges Europe and Asia — Istanbul is the only major city sitting on two continents.

countries.name: Iran
countries.fact_card: Heir to the ancient Persian Empire, with deserts, snow-capped mountains, and the world's best saffron.

countries.name: Pakistan
countries.fact_card: Home to K2, the second-highest mountain on Earth, and one of the world's most populous countries.

countries.name: Philippines
countries.fact_card: An archipelago of 7,641 islands with one of the most diverse marine ecosystems on Earth.

countries.name: Kenya
countries.fact_card: Crossed by the equator, home to the world's most famous safari grounds and the cradle of human evolution.

countries.name: Morocco
countries.fact_card: Where the Atlas Mountains meet the Sahara and the Atlantic meets the Mediterranean.

countries.name: Ethiopia
countries.fact_card: Birthplace of coffee, one of the oldest Christian nations, and home of 'Lucy,' a 3.2-million-year-old human ancestor.

countries.name: Cuba
countries.fact_card: The largest island in the Caribbean, famous for its music, vintage cars, and tropical beaches.

countries.name: Peru
countries.fact_card: Home of Machu Picchu and the Inca Empire, spanning desert coast, Andes peaks, and Amazon rainforest.

countries.name: New Zealand
countries.fact_card: Two main islands shaped by volcanoes and glaciers — home of the kiwi bird and the Māori people.
